sections.h2: Clark County offices for Vancouver owners
sections.html:
Vancouver houses are taxed by Clark County. The Treasurer, the Assessor and the Board of Equalization all work from the Public Service Center, 1300 Franklin Street, downtown. The Assessor sets value, the Treasurer sends bills and takes payment, and the Board hears appeals.

  • Treasurer: 564.397.2252, treasoff@clark.wa.gov, second-floor Joint Lobby. The lobby opens Monday through Thursday, 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Phone and email service runs Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Assessor: 564.397.2391, assessor@clark.wa.gov.
  • Board of Equalization: Suite 650, 564.397.2337, BOE@clark.wa.gov.

Vancouver is the Clark County seat, on the north bank of the Columbia River across from Portland. It had 199,698 residents in July 2025 on 48.74 square miles of land. Owners occupy 50.8 percent of homes. The median owner-occupied home is worth $462,400, median gross rent is $1,702 and median household income is $81,338.

Not every Vancouver mailing address is inside the city. Hazel Dell, Felida, Orchards and Salmon Creek are unincorporated communities just north of the city limits. Look up your parcel on the county's Property Information Center, because the levies change with the tax area.

sections.h2: What is the property tax rate in Vancouver?
sections.html:
For 2026 the county's levy report puts the total at $9.6856 per $1,000 of assessed value in tax area 037000, which covers the City of Vancouver and Vancouver School District 37. Other tax areas inside the city carry different district combinations, so trust the rate on your own statement.

Taxing district in area 037000Levy per $1,000 of assessed value
State schools2.2229
Clark County0.7416
Fort Vancouver Regional Library (general and capital facilities)0.5948
Vancouver School District 373.5186
City of Vancouver (general, affordable housing and related)2.4074
Port of Vancouver0.2002
Total9.6856

The library line combines a general rate of 0.5000 and a capital facilities rate of 0.0948.

The first half, or the full year, is due April 30. The second half is due October 31. A mailed check counts only if the Postal Service postmarks it that same day, so the county advises handing it to a post office clerk and avoiding the collection box. E-check payments online are free. First-half statements are normally available by March 15, and second-half statements by September 15.

For tax years 2023 and later, a residential parcel of four or fewer units is charged 0.75 percent a month and no penalty. Other parcels pay 1 percent a month plus penalties of 3 percent on June 1 and 8 percent on December 1.

  • Real property three or more years delinquent can be foreclosed under chapter 84.64 RCW.
  • After court proceedings begin, all taxes, interest, penalties and foreclosure costs must be paid in full before the auction.
  • Once a certificate of delinquency is filed, the Treasurer takes payment only from owners and recorded interests.
  • An income-qualified owner-occupant facing foreclosure can request a one-time waiver of interest and penalties under RCW 84.56.020(19).

If you are behind, email taxrequests@clark.wa.gov or call 564.397.2252 before you list the home.

sections.h2: Does your mortgage escrow pay Vancouver property tax?
sections.html:
More than 45 percent of Clark County homeowners pay through escrow. For those owners the county sends no statement, and you stay responsible for confirming each installment was actually paid.

Lenders occasionally pay the wrong account number or skip a payment. After April 30 and October 31, open the taxes tab on the Property Information Center and check. If a delinquency notice shows up, ask the lender which account numbers it paid and request a cancelled check or disbursement record. Confirm with the lender before sending your own money, because paying twice is a real risk.

sections.h2: How to appeal a Vancouver property value
sections.html:
Appeal to the Clark County Board of Equalization within 60 calendar days of the mailing date on your Notice of Value, or by July 1, whichever is later. Late appeals cannot be accepted, and the 60 days are counted from the notice date, not as two months. You may also file a preemptive appeal anytime from January 1 through July 1 of the assessment year.

Most Notices of Value go out in June and the rest in September, and only properties whose value changed receive one. Filing is free. A three-member citizen board hears each case in about 15 minutes and mails a written decision within 30 days. Historically, more than half of appeals end well for the owner, either after a talk with the Assessor or at the hearing.

  • Strongest evidence: comparable sales or a recent appraisal, repair bids and photographs.
  • Other properties' assessed values do not persuade the board.
  • Extra evidence has to reach the Board 21 business days before the hearing.
  • A decision can be taken to the State Board of Tax Appeals.

Clark County's senior exemption uses three income tiers. For tax years 2024 through 2026 the top income limit is $62,000, and for 2027 through 2029 it rises to $85,000 under Senate Bill 6162. For 2027 an applicant must be 61 or older, unable to work because of a disability, or rated 40 percent or higher for a service-connected disability, and must own the home and live in it at least six months of the year. Applications for 2027 open in February 2027, and current participants are adjusted automatically.

At closing, RCW 84.60.020 attaches the tax lien on January 1 and, without a contract term, divides the year by the sale date. Ask your escrow officer to confirm both halves with the Treasurer, and ask the Assessor whether an exemption or deferral ends with the sale.

sections.h2: Reading the bill before you list
sections.html:
Before you put a Vancouver house on the market, spend ten minutes with the statement. Each bill lists the taxes from every district, and the county's lookup shows whether anything is delinquent.

  • Confirm the tax area number, since it decides the rate.
  • Check both halves as paid, especially if a lender handles escrow.
  • Note any exemption on the account and ask the Assessor what ends at sale.
  • If a balance is open, email taxrequests@clark.wa.gov for a payoff before the buyer's title company asks.

A cash buyer will not need a lender's tax review, but the title company still clears the tax record, and any amount owed is paid out of your proceeds.

faqs.q: When is Vancouver, WA property tax due?
faqs.a: April 30 for the first half or the full year, and October 31 for the second half. Statements are normally available by March 15 and September 15.

faqs.q: What interest does Clark County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: For tax years 2023 and later on a residential parcel of four or fewer units, 0.75 percent per month and no penalties. Other parcels pay 1 percent per month plus 3 percent on June 1 and 8 percent on December 1.

faqs.q: How long before Clark County forecloses for unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Three years. Real property with taxes three or more years delinquent can be foreclosed. Call the Treasurer at 564.397.2252 or email taxrequests@clark.wa.gov to discuss relief.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Vancouver assessment?
faqs.a: Sixty calendar days from the mailing date on your Notice of Value, or July 1 if that is later. Late appeals cannot be accepted. Reach the Board of Equalization at 564.397.2337 or BOE@clark.wa.gov.

faqs.q: Is my Vancouver address inside city limits?
faqs.a: Not always. Hazel Dell, Felida, Orchards and Salmon Creek sit north of the city limits and are unincorporated. The Clark County Property Information Center shows which tax area applies to your parcel.
